problem.text: In rectangle $ABCD$, $AD = 1$, $P$ is on $\overline{AB}$, and $\overline{DB}$ and $\overline{DP}$ trisect $\angle ADC$. What is the perimeter of $\triangle BDP$?

steps.title: Where to start: the trisected right angle
steps.body: The clue is the word "trisect". The angle $\angle ADC$ is a corner of a rectangle, so it is $90^\circ$, and $DP$ and $DB$ cut it into three equal pieces. Equal pieces of a right angle are $30^\circ$ each, so the triangles at $D$ will be $30$-$60$-$90$ triangles, whose sides are always in the ratio $1 : \sqrt{3} : 2$ (short leg : long leg : hypotenuse).

your_turn.prompt: What are $\angle ADP$, $\angle PDB$ and $\angle BDC$?

steps.title: Triangle $BCD$ gives $BD$ and $DC$
steps.body: Triangle $BCD$ has a right angle at $C$ and $\angle BDC = 30^\circ$. The side opposite the $30^\circ$ angle is $BC$, and $BC = AD = 1$ because opposite sides of a rectangle are equal. So $BC$ is the short leg.

your_turn.prompt: Use the ratio $1 : \sqrt{3} : 2$ to find $BD$ and $DC$.

steps.title: Triangle $ADP$: watch which leg is which
steps.body: Triangle $ADP$ has a right angle at $A$ and $\angle ADP = 30^\circ$, so $\angle APD = 60^\circ$. Careful: here the known side $AD = 1$ is opposite the $60^\circ$ angle, so it is the long leg, not the short one. The short leg is $AP$, opposite the $30^\circ$ angle at $D$.

your_turn.answer: The long leg is $\sqrt{3}$ times the short leg, so $AP = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
The hypotenuse of triangle $ADP$ is $DP = 2\cdot AP = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}$. Since $AB = DC = \sqrt{3}$, we get $PB = \sqrt{3} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}$. The perimeter of $\triangle BDP$ is
$$PB + DP + BD = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3} + \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3} + 2 = 2 + \frac{4\sqrt{3}}{3}.$$ The answer is **$2 + \frac{4\sqrt{3}}{3}$**.
